Hi Samir / Edgeware team,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — good alignment on the product use cases and the latency-sensitive inference pattern you described. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a concrete Dedicated-capacity proposal and a Private/VPC path if you decide to pursue that later.

Call recap (short):
- Primary use: customer-facing assistant (real-time chat + long form summarization).
- Typical mix: frequent short prompts (UI suggestions) + occasional long-document summarization.
- Desired SLO: p95 latency target for interactive flows ~<500ms.
- Compliance flag: EU data residency + SOC2 proof required for procurement.

Asks to confirm (helps sizing):
1) Target sustained TPS and peak TPS (per-second) and expected concurrency during peaks.
2) Typical token mix: what % are short (<=150 tokens) vs long (>1k tokens); average prompt+completion token count.
3) Expected request distribution (bursty vs steady) — if you can share the 24h histogram that helps with autoscaling assumptions.
4) Any hard constraints on allowed GPU families (cost sensitivity vs low-latency preference).

I've attached a capacity worksheet (edgeware_capacity.xlsx) — if you can fill the TPS and token columns that will let us produce two concrete options: 
- Latency-optimized (lower p95, higher per-hour cost)
- Cost-optimized (higher batching, quantization, slightly higher p95)

Proposed next step: if you can reply with the TPS/concurrency/token mix today, Karthik and I will draft a two-option Dedicated sizing and an outline for a Private/VPC timeline.

Thanks —

- Peak: 120 TPS for ~10–15 minute bursts (marketing campaigns).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent open sessions ~300 users; the backend translates to ~40–60 concurrent generation requests; peak concurrency can reach ~150 concurrent generation requests.

2) Token mix:

- ~22% long jobs (document summarization, ~1.2k–3k tokens end-to-end).

3) Distribution: bursty — we have predictable campaign windows. I'll attach a 7-day minute-level histogram (edgeware_traffic.csv).

4) GPU constraints: we prefer to evaluate Dedicated first. Cost is important for us, but latency is a hard constraint for the interactive flows. We have internal budget conversations around H100 adoption — curious about H100 vs A100 tradeoffs for this workload.

Hi all — reviewed the histogram and the worksheet. High level recommendations below; numbers are conservative estimates for initial sizing. I'll run final calc in capacity_calc_v2.xlsx (attached).

Executive summary:
- For their workload (mixed short + long, EU residency, hard p95 target), I recommend we lead with an H100 80GB Dedicated cluster for the latency-optimized option and an A100 80GB cluster for cost-optimized. H100 gives ~20–30% lower token latency on long-context workloads and better memory for larger KV caches (helpful for summarization jobs).

Option A — Latency-optimized
- Hardware: H100 80GB nodes (NVIDIA H100 SXM).
- Per-GPU practical sustained throughput (short prompts): ~18–22 effective TPS (single model, warm cache, small batching, concurrency 6–8).
- For 45 sustained TPS + 120 TPS peak: recommend 6 H100 GPUs (capacity headroom for bursts & maintenance).
- Concurrency: plan for 8 concurrent streams per GPU for interactive flows; long jobs routed to a small job pool (2–3 GPUs) to avoid tail latency impact.
- Quantization: prefer FP16 for latency path; avoid aggressive q4 quant for long-document quality-sensitive summaries.
- Estimated committed monthly cost (incl. infra & managed runtime): ballpark $68k–$95k/month (final depends on region prices & reserved term).

Option B — Cost-optimized
- Hardware: A100 80GB (or similarly provisioned Ampere instances).
- Per-GPU practical sustained throughput (short prompts): ~12–16 TPS with larger batching and q4_0 quantization for shorter prompts.
- For 45 sustained TPS + 120 TPS peak: recommend 8 A100 GPUs (autoscaling burst policy to spin additional capacity for campaign windows).
- Concurrency: batch sizes larger; concurrency per GPU higher (12–16) but expect higher p95 (~600–750ms) for interactive flows.
- Quantization: q4_0 or q5x for cost path for short prompts; keep FP16 or mixed for long summarizations on a small subset of GPUs.
- Estimated committed monthly cost: ballpark $42k–$60k/month.

Operational notes and follow-ups:
- KV cache sizing: pre-warm short-session KV cache on the latency pool; keep long-job pool isolated to avoid cache thrashing.
- Fallbacks: we can propose routing policy to shift long jobs to Dedicated burst nodes or to Redwood Hosted during extreme peaks for elasticity.
- Compliance: Priya — we should bundle SOC2 evidence + EU region deployment notes in the proposal; recommend a short security addendum for procurement.

Samir — if you’re OK with these two options I suggest we:
1) Schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive next week (Karthik + our infra lead) to validate numbers and run a small synthetic benchmark on a representative prompt set.
2) Share the capacity_calc_v2.xlsx with a line-by-line cost table and assumptions.

Happy to walk through details — I’ll attach the calc and a short runbook.

Thanks,
